**EDITED**

Per the response to this review, I called the store and spoke to a very helpful and professional manager. She apologized, gave me the names of the fish experts she trusts at this location, and reassured me that she would be speaking to the staff members with whom I had the poor interactions. She also provided a full refund for the deceased fish. While the initial experience was unplesant, I am updating my review to reflect the fact that the manger took ownership of the situation and worked quickly and diligently to make it right.

**Original Review**

Everyone in this store has always been incredibly friendly and kind. However, it seems everyone's knowledge is not equal, and I have to caution customers against seeking advice from the fish department. My partner and I went in looking to purchase fish for the first time, and made it very clear that we knew nothing. We were advised to set up our tank, leave it running for a week, and come back to purchase our fish. We asked if there was additional research we should do, and, crucially, the staff said no. We did what we were told and came back, they tested our water, and told us we were good to go. We asked if this was long enough for the tank to have cycled and made it safe, they said absolutely. We then purchased 11 fish. One fish died each of the first 5 days. I went back and explained this, and nobody mentioned that they have a fish exchange policy. They just tested our water again, told us to buy some test strips on our own, and said that maybe the type of fish (all guppies at this point) were just weak. After much more research online, we learned that the tank was absolutely not cycled in just one week without fish or any other bio material, 11 fish was probably too many to add at once, and the test strips we were advised to buy (that the store itself uses) are poor quality and don't even mention ammonia, one of the leading killers of fish. We went back and bought a much more comprehensive water testing kit, and sure enough - ammonia levels were off the charts and it was a shock any of the fish were still alive. I started doing my own research on how to cycle a tank while the fish are in it (not recommended due to stress and casualties) and thought everything was in hand. Then, about a week ago, one of the surviving fish came down with a bad case of ich, due to stress from the poor water parameters we were told not to worry about. At my wit's end, I went back and talked with the original person who sold us our fish. He said "sorry, most fish get ich." I expressed my frustration with the misguidance/lack of information that killed 5 fish and got this 6th one sick, to which this staff member responded "well we don't really cycle, if you put in the daily dose of stability they just don't die". I told him I had followed the dosing instructions for stability to a T, and half my tank had died anyway. He then said "well didn't I tell you we have a fish exchange program? if your fish die you can bring in their bodies to exchange them". Nobody had mentioned this in the now nearly 5 visits we had paid to this  location. I had, of course, disposed of the fish bodies to avoid them decomposing in the tank. When I said this, he said "well that's a bummer, we can't do anything without the bodies". I then tried to explain, with as much sympathy for this employee as possible, that all of these fish had died because of the poor advice we got from him/this pet supplies plus location. He then said "well what do you want us to do?" At that point, I didn't feel confident in my ability to remain composed so I purchased the only ich cure they had in stock and went home to administer the treatment. That fish finally passed about a week later, after an obviously agonizing battle. Now I have to wait to see if any of the other survivors are infected, as over half of my tank is dead...
